checks.label: A three by three determinant is obtained by multiplying each element of the first row by its corresponding cofactor and then adding the three together: on each screen that works one out, the minors and the total drawn are that sum, it agrees with the full six-term formula, and the box drawn has that volume

Any transformation that inverts the orientation of space has a negative determinant: with k's tip pushed below the floor the box comes out mirrored and its volume reads negative, and lifted back above the floor it reads positive again

The cross product is really the determinant of a grid with i, j and k in its top row: on each cross product screen the cofactors are the parts of the arrow drawn, they match the part by part formula, and the arrow stands square to both rows
With i and j on the floor the volume is the height: wherever k's tip is dragged, the volume shown is k's up part, the third column is k's tip, and sliding it sideways leaves the volume alone
Dropping k's tip to the floor squashes the box flat: the volume reads 0, every point of space lands on the floor, and the puzzle's flat pick lies on the floor too

Every worked number is right: minors 6, 2 and 0 give 10, and the box's floor 5 times height 2 agrees (14 without the minus); minors 3, 2 and 1 give 7 (11 without the minus, 12 down the diagonal); a × b = 5k and j × i = −k; the circuit's grid has 6, 12 and −3, minors 63, −18 and 9, and 378 − 54 = 324 (432 without the minus); r × F = 45k (51 from the whole 170 N); [1 2 3; 4 5 6; 7 8 9] has minors −3, −6 and −3 and gives 0 (−24 without the minus, 45 down the diagonal); k on (2, −1, 3) gives 3 (6 and 4 are slips)
Each puzzle's answer comes from the rule, and each wrong answer offered is the slip its hint names
Each puzzle offers three different answers, accepts only the right one, and draws every wrong one in the warning colour
Before Check, no puzzle shows its answer; after a right answer, it does

Each demonstration ends where the lesson says: k on (1, 0.5, 2) with volume 2, then slid to (−1, 1, 2) keeping volume 2 all the way, then dropped to the floor with volume 0; the recipe's box on [2 1 1; 1 3 0; 0 0 2] with volume 10; a × b standing at 5k
Every demonstration has finished arriving within its 3 to 4.5 s, none starting before the 0.35 s screen fade ends; every answer's motion, right or wrong, within 2.5 s
